source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ מָק֣וֹר נִפְתָּ֔ח לְבֵ֥ית דָּוִ֖יד וּלְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לְחַטַּ֖את וּלְנִדָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: On that day there will be a fountain opened for [the] house of David and for [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

en.L: In that day there will be a fountain opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.
en.B: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to wash away their sin and impurity.
en.R: At that time a spring will be opened for the family of David and the people of Jerusalem. Its water will wash away their sin and make them clean.

pt.L: Naquele dia haverá uma fonte aberta para a casa de Davi e para os habitantes de Jerusalém, para o pecado e para a impureza.
pt.B: Naquele dia uma fonte será aberta para a casa de Davi e para o povo de Jerusalém, para lavar o seu pecado e a sua impureza.
pt.R: Naquele dia uma fonte vai ser aberta para a família de Davi e para o povo de Jerusalém. A água dela vai lavar o pecado deles e deixá-los puros.

decisions.choice: a fountain for sin and for impurity: water that cleanses
decisions.reason: The law used water to cleanse from uncleanness: "water for impurity", mixed with the ashes of a red heifer, cleansed those who had touched a dead body (Numbers 19:9-21). The word for "impurity" is the one used there; it also means the uncleanness of a woman's monthly period (Leviticus 15:19-24) and, in the prophets, the uncleanness of sin and idol worship (Ezekiel 36:17). Here God opens a spring that never runs dry, for cleansing from sin itself.

decisions.choice: on that day ... a fountain opened: the people who mourned in 12:10-14 are cleansed
decisions.reason: The same house of David and people of Jerusalem who mourned for the one they pierced (12:10) are now given cleansing. Ezekiel 36:25 promises, "I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean", and the picture of water flowing from Jerusalem returns in 14:8 (compare Ezekiel 47:1-12; Joel 4:18).

decisions.choice: to wash away (B); Its water will wash away ... make them clean (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "for sin and for impurity". Balanced and Readable say what the fountain is for (m1).

decisions.choice: uma fonte; o pecado e a impureza
decisions.reason: "Fonte" at every level, the plain word for water that springs up; "impureza" is the Old Testament terms' word for ritual uncleanness (m1), and Readable says "puros", as the terms set "puro" and "impuro".

source.text: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם׀יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אַכְרִ֞ית אֶת־שְׁמ֤וֹת הָֽעֲצַבִּים֙ מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יִזָּכְר֖וּ ע֑וֹד וְגַ֧ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־ר֥וּחַ הַטֻּמְאָ֖ה אַעֲבִ֥יר מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on that day, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, [that] I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will not be remembered again; and also the prophets and the spirit of the uncleanness I will cause to pass from the land.

en.L: And it will be in that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, [that] I will cut off the idols' names from the land, and they will not be remembered again; and also the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness I will remove from the land.
en.B: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, I will wipe out the names of the idols from the land, and no one will remember them any more. The prophets too, and the spirit of impurity, I will remove from the land.
en.R: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, I will get rid of the idols in the land, and no one will even remember their names. I will also remove the false prophets from the land, and the spirit that makes people unclean.

pt.L: E acontecerá naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, [que] eliminarei da terra os nomes dos ídolos, e não serão mais lembrados; e também os profetas e o espírito da impureza farei sair da terra.
pt.B: Naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, apagarei da terra os nomes dos ídolos, e ninguém se lembrará mais deles. Também os profetas e o espírito de impureza removerei da terra.
pt.R: Naquele dia, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, vou acabar com os ídolos da terra, e ninguém vai nem se lembrar do nome deles. Vou tirar da terra também os falsos profetas e o espírito que faz as pessoas ficarem impuras.

decisions.choice: cut off the names of the idols, and they will not be remembered: idol worship will end completely
decisions.reason: To call on a god's name was to worship it. Israel was told not even to mention the names of other gods (Exodus 23:13), and Hosea 2:19 promises that the names of the Baals will be forgotten. When the names are no longer spoken, the worship is gone.

decisions.choice: the prophets: those who prophesy falsely
decisions.reason: The prophets removed here are named with the idols and "the spirit of uncleanness", and verses 3-6 show that they speak lies in the LORD's name. They are false prophets, like those Jeremiah opposed (Jeremiah 23:9-40; 27:9-10). The Hebrew does not add "false"; the context makes it plain.

decisions.choice: the spirit of uncleanness: the power behind false prophecy and idol worship
decisions.reason: It stands against the "spirit of grace" the LORD pours out in 12:10. 1 Kings 22:22-23 tells of a "lying spirit" in the mouths of prophets. The LORD will remove the spirit that made his people unclean, as the fountain of verse 1 washes them.

decisions.choice: And it will be in that day, declares the LORD of hosts (L); On that day, declares the LORD of Armies (B); At that time, says the LORD of Armies (R); false prophets (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas follow the wording set in Isaiah. Readable adds "false" to make plain which prophets are meant (m2).

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יִנָּבֵ֣א אִישׁ֮ עוֹד֒ וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵ֠לָיו אָבִ֨יו וְאִמּ֤וֹ יֹֽלְדָיו֙ לֹ֣א תִֽחְיֶ֔ה כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וּדְקָרֻ֜הוּ אָבִ֧יהוּ וְאִמּ֛וֹ יֹלְדָ֖יו בְּהִנָּבְאֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, if prophesies a man again, then will say to him his father and his mother who bore him, You will not live, for falsehood you have spoken in [the] name of Yahweh; and will pierce him his father and his mother who bore him when he prophesies.

en.L: And it will be, if anyone prophesies again, his father and his mother who bore him will say to him, "You shall not live, for you have spoken falsehood in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}"; then his father and his mother who bore him will pierce him through when he prophesies.
en.B: If anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother will say to him, "You must not live, because you have spoken lies in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And when he prophesies, his own father and mother will run him through.
en.R: If anyone still claims to speak for God, his own parents will say to him, "You must die, because you have told lies and said they came from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And when he prophesies, his own father and mother will stab him to death.

pt.L: E acontecerá que, se alguém ainda profetizar, o seu pai e a sua mãe, que o geraram, lhe dirão: "Você não viverá, porque falou mentira em nome {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}"; e o seu pai e a sua mãe, que o geraram, o traspassarão quando ele profetizar.
pt.B: Se alguém ainda profetizar, o seu próprio pai e a sua própria mãe lhe dirão: "Você não pode viver, porque falou mentiras em nome {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}." E, quando ele profetizar, o seu próprio pai e a sua própria mãe o traspassarão.
pt.R: Se alguém ainda disser que fala em nome de Deus, os seus próprios pais vão dizer a ele: "Você tem de morrer, porque contou mentiras e disse que elas vinham {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}." E, quando ele profetizar, o seu próprio pai e a sua própria mãe vão matá-lo a facadas.

decisions.choice: his father and his mother will say, You shall not live: the law on false prophets
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 13:7-12 and 18:20 say that a prophet who speaks in the name of other gods, or claims to speak in the LORD's name what he has not commanded, must die, and that no one, not even a close relative, may shield him. Here the false prophet's own parents carry out the law. Their loyalty to the LORD will outweigh even their love for their son.

decisions.choice: pierce him through: the verb of 12:10
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 12:10, "the one they pierced". The parents run their son through with a sword or spear. The picture is extreme, and it shows how completely false prophecy will be rejected on that day.

decisions.choice: his own father and mother (B); his own parents (R); run him through (B); stab him to death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "his own" to bring out the force of "who bore him", and leave out the repeated phrase the second time. Readable says "claims to speak for God" for "prophesies" at the start, and "You must die" for "You shall not live". The man is a son of his father and mother, so no gender setting is used.

decisions.choice: traspassarão (L, B)
decisions.reason: The verb of 12:10 (m2), so Literal and Balanced keep "traspassar", the word set there, and the echo is heard; Readable says what is done, as the English Readable does (r-en-1).

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יֵבֹ֧שׁוּ הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ מֵחֶזְיֹנ֖וֹ בְּהִנָּֽבְאֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֧א יִלְבְּשׁ֛וּ אַדֶּ֥רֶת שֵׂעָ֖ר לְמַ֥עַן כַּחֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on that day [that] will be ashamed the prophets, each of his vision when he prophesies; and they will not put on a cloak of hair in order to deceive.

en.L: And it will be in that day [that] the prophets will be ashamed, each of his vision when he prophesies; and they will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
en.B: On that day every prophet will be ashamed of the vision he prophesies, and they will not put on a prophet's hairy cloak to deceive people.
en.R: At that time the prophets will be ashamed of their visions and of what they say. They will no longer wear a prophet's coat made of hair to trick people.

pt.L: E acontecerá naquele dia [que] os profetas se envergonharão, cada um da sua visão quando profetizar; e não vestirão um manto de pelos para enganar.
pt.B: Naquele dia, cada profeta terá vergonha da visão que profetiza, e eles não vestirão o manto de pelos dos profetas para enganar as pessoas.
pt.R: Naquele dia, os profetas vão ter vergonha das suas visões e do que dizem. Eles não vão mais usar a capa de pelos dos profetas para enganar as pessoas.

decisions.choice: a hairy cloak: the dress of a prophet
decisions.reason: Elijah was known by his hairy garment and leather belt (2 Kings 1:8), and his cloak passed to Elisha (1 Kings 19:19; 2 Kings 2:13-14). John the Baptist dressed the same way (Matthew 3:4). False prophets wore it to look like true ones. The word for cloak is the one translated "glory" in 11:3.

decisions.choice: the prophets will be ashamed, each of his vision: they will not want to be known as prophets
decisions.reason: On that day the false prophets will be ashamed of their visions and will hide that they ever were prophets, as verses 5-6 show.

decisions.choice: a prophet's hairy cloak (B); a prophet's coat made of hair (R); to deceive people (B); to trick people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose cloak it was (m1) and whom the prophets deceive. Readable makes the visions plural, "their visions".

decisions.choice: um manto de pelos (L, B); a capa de pelos (R)
decisions.reason: The prophet's dress (m1) is "manto", the word for Elijah's cloak in 2 Kings 2:13 in Portuguese; Readable says "capa", the everyday word.

source.text: וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א נָבִ֖יא אָנֹ֑כִי אִישׁ־עֹבֵ֤ד אֲדָמָה֙ אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אָדָ֖ם הִקְנַ֥נִי מִנְּעוּרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will say, Not a prophet [am] I; a man working [the] ground [am] I, for a man acquired me from my youth.

en.L: And he will say, "I [am] not a prophet; I [am] a man who works the ground, for a man bought me in my youth."
en.B: Each will say, "I am no prophet. I work the soil; I was sold to a man as a servant when I was young."
en.R: Each of them will say, "I am not a prophet. I am a farmer. Someone bought me as a servant when I was young, and I have worked the land ever since."

pt.L: E ele dirá: "Eu não [sou] profeta; eu [sou] um homem que lavra a terra, porque um homem me comprou na minha juventude."
pt.B: Cada um dirá: "Não sou profeta. Eu trabalho a terra; fui vendido a um homem como servo quando era jovem."
pt.R: Cada um deles vai dizer: "Não sou profeta. Sou agricultor. Alguém me comprou como servo quando eu era jovem, e desde então trabalho na terra."

decisions.choice: I am not a prophet: the words of Amos, used to deny the calling
decisions.reason: Amos told the priest of Bethel, "I am not a prophet, nor a member of a company of prophets; I am a herdsman" (Amos 7:14). Amos meant that the LORD had called him from his work. The false prophet uses the same words to hide what he had been.

decisions.choice: a man bought me in my youth: following the Hebrew text
alternatives: the land has been my possession since my youth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "a man acquired me (as a servant) from my youth". He claims that he has always worked the land for a master, and so had no time to be a prophet. Some read the same letters as "the ground has been my possession from my youth", that is, "I have been a farmer all my life". The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: Each will say (B); Each of them will say (R); as a servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "each" for the singular "he", since verse 4 speaks of every prophet, and add "as a servant" to explain "bought me" (m2).

decisions.choice: Eu não sou profeta (every level)
decisions.reason: The words of Amos 7:14 (m1), with no article, the way Portuguese denies a calling, so that the echo of Amos is heard.

source.text: וְאָמַ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו מָ֧ה הַמַּכּ֛וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה בֵּ֣ין יָדֶ֑יךָ וְאָמַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכֵּ֖יתִי בֵּ֥ית מְאַהֲבָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And [one] will say to him, What [are] the wounds these between your hands? And he will say, [Those with] which I was struck [at the] house of my friends.

en.L: And [someone] will say to him, "What [are] these wounds between your hands?" And he will say, "[Those] with which I was struck [in] the house of my friends."
en.B: And if someone asks him, "Then what are these wounds on your chest?" he will answer, "I got them in the house of my friends."
en.R: If someone asks him, "Then what are these wounds on your chest?" he will say, "I was hurt at my friends' house."

pt.L: E [alguém] lhe dirá: "Que [são] estas feridas entre as suas mãos?" E ele dirá: "[São aquelas] com que fui ferido [na] casa dos meus amigos."
pt.B: E, se alguém lhe perguntar: "Então que feridas são essas no seu peito?", ele responderá: "Eu as recebi na casa dos meus amigos."
pt.R: Se alguém perguntar a ele: "Então que feridas são essas no seu peito?", ele vai dizer: "Eu me machuquei na casa dos meus amigos."

decisions.choice: wounds between your hands: wounds on the chest or back
decisions.reason: "Between the hands" means the body between the arms, the chest or the back (2 Kings 9:24 uses the phrase of an arrow that struck the king between his shoulders). Prophets of Baal cut themselves in their frenzy (1 Kings 18:28), and the law forbade such cutting (Leviticus 19:28; Deuteronomy 14:1). The scars would give away that the man had been such a prophet.

decisions.choice: in the house of my friends: an excuse, perhaps a pun
decisions.reason: The man explains his scars as wounds from a quarrel among friends. The word for "friends" means "those who love me", and the prophets use it of the lovers Israel ran after, its false gods (Hosea 2:7; Jeremiah 22:20), so the excuse may give away the truth.

decisions.choice: the wounds of a false prophet, not a prophecy of Christ
decisions.reason: Older translations read "wounds in your hands", and some Christian readers took the verse as a prophecy of the wounds of Christ. In its setting the speaker is a false prophet who denies what he has been (verses 4-5), and his wounds are on his body, not his hands. The New Testament does not quote this verse. The next verse turns to the LORD's shepherd.

decisions.choice: on your chest (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "between your hands" (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase.

decisions.choice: no seu peito (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "between your hands", the body between the arms (m1), as the English does (r-en-1); Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase. People speak to each other with "você".

source.text: חֶ֗רֶב עוּרִ֤י עַל־רֹעִי֙ וְעַל־גֶּ֣בֶר עֲמִיתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת הַ֤ךְ אֶת־הָֽרֹעֶה֙ וּתְפוּצֶ֣יןָ הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֥י יָדִ֖י עַל־הַצֹּעֲרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Sword, awake against my shepherd, and against [the] man [who is] my associate, declaration of Yahweh of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and will be scattered the sheep; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.

en.L: Sword, awake against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherd, and against the man [who is] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} associate, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts. \q Strike the shepherd, and let the sheep be scattered; \q and I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand upon the small ones.
en.B: Awake, sword, against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherd, against the man who stands next to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter; \q I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against even the little ones.
en.R: Sword, wake up and attack {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} shepherd, the man who is close to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. \q Kill the shepherd, and the sheep will run off in every direction. \q I will turn against even the weakest of the flock.

pt.L: Espada, desperta contra o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} pastor, e contra o homem [que é] o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} companheiro, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos. \q Fere o pastor, e que as ovelhas sejam dispersadas; \q e voltarei a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão contra os pequeninos.
pt.B: Desperta, espada, contra o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} pastor, contra o homem que está ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} lado, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos. \q Fere o pastor, e as ovelhas se espalharão; \q voltarei a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão até contra os pequeninos.
pt.R: Espada, acorda e ataca o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} pastor, o homem que é chegado a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos. \q Mata o pastor, e as ovelhas vão fugir para todos os lados. \q Vou me voltar até contra as mais fracas do rebanho.

decisions.choice: Sword, awake against my shepherd: the LORD himself calls for his shepherd to be struck
decisions.reason: The LORD calls on the sword as if it were a person, as in Jeremiah 47:6. The shepherd is "my shepherd", one the LORD appointed. The verses do not say who he is. Many read him as the good shepherd rejected in 11:4-14, whom the people valued at thirty pieces of silver; some take him as the worthless shepherd of 11:17, and some move verses 7-9 to follow 11:17. "The man who is my associate" fits a shepherd close to the LORD better than a worthless one.

decisions.choice: the man who is my associate: one who stands beside the LORD as a near companion
decisions.reason: The word is rare. It is used in Leviticus for one's fellow or neighbor, a near equal (Leviticus 5:21; 19:11, 15; 25:14-17). Here it is the LORD who calls the shepherd his "associate", a man closely bound to him.

decisions.choice: I will turn my hand against the little ones: judgment that falls on the weak of the flock too
decisions.reason: To turn one's hand against someone is to act against them (Amos 1:8). The "little ones" are the young and weak of the flock (Jeremiah 49:20). When the shepherd is struck, the flock suffers too; verses 8-9 show that the judgment also refines a remnant. Isaiah 1:25 uses the same phrase for the LORD's purifying of his people.

decisions.choice: Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered: quoted by Jesus in Matthew 26:31 and Mark 14:27
decisions.reason: On the night of his arrest Jesus quotes these words of himself and his disciples, who will all leave him. In the Gospels' wording God himself says "I will strike the shepherd". In the Hebrew the LORD commands the sword to strike, so in both he is the one behind the striking.

decisions.choice: my shepherd, my associate, my hand (deity_pronoun setting); the shepherd (no setting)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of himself, so "my", "me" and "my hand" take the deity_pronoun setting. The shepherd takes none, as the pierced one of 12:10 and the king of 9:9 do not: the text does not settle who he is (m1).

decisions.choice: the man who stands next to me (B); the man who is close to me (R); Kill (R); run off in every direction (R); against even the weakest of the flock (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain "associate" (m2). Readable says "Kill" for "Strike", as the sword strikes to kill, and explains "the little ones" (m3). "Declares the LORD of hosts" follows the wording set in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: Fere o pastor, e que as ovelhas sejam dispersadas (L); Fere o pastor, e as ovelhas se espalharão (B); Mata o pastor, e as ovelhas vão fugir para todos os lados (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew 26:31 quotes these words (m4), so each level keeps its Portuguese where the Hebrew is the same: "ferir o pastor", "dispersadas" (L), "se espalharão" (B), "vão fugir para todos os lados" (R). The Gospel follows the Greek, "Ferirei", God striking; the Hebrew has the LORD command the sword (m1), so Portuguese follows it with "Fere", the "tu" imperative to the sword, feminine in Portuguese as in Hebrew. Readable says "Mata", as the English Readable says "Kill" (r-en-2).

decisions.choice: o meu pastor, o meu companheiro, a minha mão (deity_pronoun spans); the shepherd takes none
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): the LORD speaks of himself, so "meu", "mim" and "minha" take the span; the shepherd, whom the text does not name, takes none. "Companheiro" (L) is the near fellow of Leviticus (m2); Balanced and Readable say how close he is.

source.text: וְהָיָ֤ה בְכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֣יִם בָּ֔הּ יִכָּרְת֖וּ יִגְוָ֑עוּ וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית יִוָּ֥תֶר בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in all the land, declaration of Yahweh, [that] two portions in it will be cut off [and] perish, and the third will be left in it.

en.L: And it will be in all the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q [that] two parts in it will be cut off [and] perish, \q and the third will be left in it.
en.B: In the whole land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q two-thirds will be cut off and die, \q but one-third will be left in it.
en.R: In the whole land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q two out of every three people will be killed, \q and only one out of three will be left alive.

pt.L: E acontecerá em toda a terra, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q [que] duas partes dela serão eliminadas [e] perecerão, \q e a terceira será deixada nela.
pt.B: Em toda a terra, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q dois terços serão eliminados e morrerão, \q mas um terço será deixado nela.
pt.R: Em toda a terra, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q de cada três pessoas, duas vão ser mortas, \q e só uma vai ficar viva.

decisions.choice: two parts: two-thirds
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a mouth of two", an idiom for a double share or two portions (Deuteronomy 21:17; 2 Kings 2:9). With "the third" that follows, it means two of three parts.

decisions.choice: two-thirds cut off, one-third left: a remnant survives the judgment
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 5:1-12 divides the people into thirds, with only a few saved. Here the third that is left becomes the purified people of verse 9. The numbers stress how severe the judgment is, and that a remnant remains.

decisions.choice: two parts ... the third (L); two-thirds ... one-third (B); two out of every three ... one out of three (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "two parts"; Balanced and Readable give the fractions (m1). "Declares the LORD" follows the wording set in Isaiah.

source.text: וְהֵבֵאתִ֤י אֶת־הַשְּׁלִשִׁית֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וּצְרַפְתִּים֙ כִּצְרֹ֣ף אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּבְחַנְתִּ֖ים כִּבְחֹ֣ן אֶת־הַזָּהָ֑ב ה֣וּא׀יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֗י וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶעֱנֶ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ אָמַ֨רְתִּי֙ עַמִּ֣י ה֔וּא וְה֥וּא יֹאמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will bring the third into the fire, and I will refine them as one refines the silver, and I will test them as one tests the gold. It will call on my name, and I will answer it; I will say, My people [is] it; and it will say, Yahweh [is] my God.

en.L: And I will bring the third into the fire, \q and refine them as one refines silver, \q and test them as one tests gold. \q It will call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will answer it; \q I will say, "My people [is] it," \q and it will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] my God."
en.B: I will bring this third through the fire; \q I will refine them as silver is refined \q and test them as one tests gold. \q They will call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and I will answer. \q I will say, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people," \q and they will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my God."
en.R: I will put the third that is left through the fire. \q I will make them pure, as silver is made pure, \q and test them, as gold is tested. \q They will pray to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will answer them. \q I will say, "These are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people." \q And each of them will say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is my God."

pt.L: E levarei a terceira parte ao fogo, \q e a refinarei como se refina a prata, \q e a provarei como se prova o ouro. \q Ela invocará o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome, e eu lhe responderei; \q eu direi: "Ela [é] o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo", \q e ela dirá: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} [é] o meu Deus."
pt.B: Farei essa terceira parte passar pelo fogo; \q eu a refinarei como se refina a prata \q e a provarei como se prova o ouro. \q Eles invocarão o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome, e eu responderei. \q Direi: "Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo", \q e eles dirão: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é o meu Deus."
pt.R: Vou fazer a terça parte que restar passar pelo fogo. \q Vou purificá-los como se purifica a prata \q e prová-los como se prova o ouro. \q Eles vão orar a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, e eu vou responder. \q Eu vou dizer: "Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo." \q E cada um deles vai dizer: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} é o meu Deus."

decisions.choice: refine them as silver, test them as gold: the fire purifies
decisions.reason: Silver and gold were melted in a furnace so that the waste rose to the top and could be removed, leaving the pure metal (Proverbs 17:3). The prophets use the picture of God purifying his people through suffering (Isaiah 1:25; 48:10; Malachi 3:2-3; Psalm 66:10). 1 Peter 1:7 uses it of faith tested by trials.

decisions.choice: They are my people ... The LORD is my God: the covenant words spoken again
decisions.reason: These are the words of the covenant between the LORD and Israel (Leviticus 26:12; Jeremiah 31:33). Hosea 1:9 had denied them, and Hosea 2:25 restored them in the same exchange: "You are my people", "My God". The purified remnant is the covenant people again.

decisions.choice: it will call ... it will say: the remnant spoken of as one
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of "the third" as one person: "it will call", "I will answer it", "my people is it", "it will say, my God". The remnant speaks as one, and the last words, "my God", are each one's confession.

decisions.choice: call on my name (L, B); pray to me (R); my God; each of them (R)
decisions.reason: "Call on the name" of the LORD is to pray to him and worship him (Genesis 4:26; Joel 3:5); Readable says "pray to me". The LORD speaks of his own name and people, so "my" and "me" take the deity_pronoun setting; "my God" is the people's word and takes none. Literal keeps the Hebrew singular, "it"; Balanced and Readable say "they" and "these", and Readable adds "each of them" to explain "my" (m3).

decisions.choice: a terceira parte ... ela (L); eles (B, R); invocará o meu nome (L, B), orar a mim (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the remnant as one, "ela", agreeing with "a terceira parte", as the Hebrew speaks of it as one (m3); Balanced and Readable say "eles", as the English does. The covenant words (m2) are "o meu povo" and "o meu Deus" at every level, as the covenant formula sets them in Portuguese.
